= Fork governance — this repository reports its conformance on every pull request
:toc: none
:revdate: 2026-10-24

Every pull request in this repository carries one comment titled *Fork
governance*. It is regenerated in place on every push, and it reports three
lanes, in this order:

[cols="1,4",options="header"]
|===
| Lane | What it tells you
| DEED syntax | whether the repository's `.deed` self-description still parses
| K9-DEED conformance | whether its committed K9 contracts pass layers L0–L2
| Hypatia verdict grid | what the scanners ran and what each of them reported
|===

The comment opens with a summary table, then the k9-deed grid, then the
Hypatia grid. A row that is *orange* means the evidence is missing, not that
the check passed. Nothing in the comment is a security certification.

== Where the normative documentation lives

All of it, in AsciiDoc, in one place:

https://github.com/metadatastician/standards/tree/main/3-practice/fork-governance

* `README.adoc` — what the system is and how to read a row
* `SPEC.adoc` — the normative comment contract (markers, order, states)
* `LANES.adoc` — each lane's implementation, artifacts and permissions
* `ADOPTION.adoc` — how to turn it on in another repository
* `DISCOVERY.adoc` — this chain, and what keeps it from rotting

== If the comment is missing

The comment is produced by `.github/workflows/fork-governance.yml` in this
repository. If a pull request has no such comment, that workflow did not run
on it — which is a defect in this repository, not an absence of findings. Check
the Actions tab for a run named *Fork governance*.
